name: John
description: Prophet living at the time of the New Testament

points: His raiment of camel's hair and the leathern girdle about his loins are not incidental. That was Elijah's manner, and it marks John as coming in the same spirit.

note.label: Matthew 3: John the Baptist and the Baptism of the Holy Ghost and Fire

points: John is cast into prison and Christ departs into Galilee, and dwells in Capernaum in the borders of Zebulun and Nephthalim.

note.label: Matthew 4: The Temptation in the Wilderness and the Calling of the Fishers

points: John hears in the prison the works of Christ and sends two of his disciples to ask, Art thou he that should come, or do we look for another?

note.label: Matthew 11: Art Thou He That Should Come

points: Among them that are born of women there hath not risen a greater than John the Baptist, notwithstanding he that is least in the kingdom of heaven is greater than he.

note.label: Matthew 11: Art Thou He That Should Come

points: Read above verse 14 so we know the context. “Verily I say unto you, Among them that are born of women there hath not risen a greater than John the Baptist:” Christ said there's nobody greater than John the Baptist. “notwithstanding he that is least in the kingdom of heaven is greater than he.” Why? Because in the kingdom of heaven, when you read Isaiah, all Israel shall be all righteous: no fears, no more sin. That's why the least in the kingdom is going to be greater than John was at that time.

note.label: The Gospel Is Black Liberation

points: And from the days of John the Baptist until now. From the days of John the Baptist until the time of Christ.

note.label: The Waters of Noah Will Be Fire

points: From the days of John the Baptist until now the kingdom of heaven suffereth violence, and the violent take it by force. The kingdom of heaven here is the children of Israel; we are the kingdom of heaven. The violent at that time were the Romans, and the violent have taken the kingdom by force.

note.label: Nolan Wells: The Perpetual Hatred We Never Learned

points: From the days of John the Baptist the kingdom of heaven suffereth violence, and the violent take it by force.

note.label: Transforming From Immorality To Beautiful Civility Returning Our Kingdom To An Organized Nation Pt 3

points: From the days of John the Baptist until now the kingdom of heaven suffereth violence, and the violent take it by force.

note.label: Matthew 11: Art Thou He That Should Come

points: “And from the days of John the Baptist until now the kingdom of heaven suffereth violence,” By Rome, at the hands of Rome. “and the violent take it by force.” How did Rome get over Jerusalem? Around 63 BC General Pompey came in with a whole military and took Jerusalem, took the land of Israel. That's how Rome got their foothold on the land, so that's why when Christ was born they all had to pay taxes to Caesar.

note.label: The Gospel Is Black Liberation

points: All the prophets and the law prophesied until John, and if ye will receive it, this is Elias which was for to come.

note.label: Matthew 11: Art Thou He That Should Come

points: John came neither eating nor drinking and they said he hath a devil; the Son of man came eating and drinking and they called him a gluttonous man. Nothing would have satisfied them.

note.label: Matthew 11: Art Thou He That Should Come

points: Asked by what authority he does these things, he asks them first whether the baptism of John was from heaven or of men.

note.label: Matthew 21: The King Cometh Meek, and the Kingdom Taken Away

points: John came in the way of righteousness and they believed him not, and when they had seen it they repented not afterward that they might believe him.

note.label: Matthew 21: The King Cometh Meek, and the Kingdom Taken Away

points: John preached the baptism of repentance for the remission of sins.

note.label: The Mercy and Humility of King Manasseh

points: Herod hears of him and says it is John, whom he beheaded, risen from the dead.

note.label: Mark 6: A Prophet Without Honour, the Death of John, and the Five Thousand

points: John had told Herod plainly, It is not lawful for thee to have thy brother's wife. Herod knew the law well enough to be accused by it, because those rulers were schooled in the customs of Israel.

note.label: Mark 6: A Prophet Without Honour, the Death of John, and the Five Thousand

points: When the oath is made, the daughter asks her mother what to ask, and is told, The head of John the Baptist. The king was exceeding sorry, but for his oath's sake he sent the executioner.

note.label: Mark 6: A Prophet Without Honour, the Death of John, and the Five Thousand

points: John's disciples ask, Art thou he that should come? and in that same hour he cured many, and answered by the works: the blind see, the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised, to the poor the gospel is preached.

note.label: Luke 7: Great Faith, the Widow's Son, and the Woman Who Loved Much

points: Among those that are born of women there is not a greater prophet than John the Baptist, but he that is least in the kingdom of God is greater than he.

note.label: Luke 7: Great Faith, the Widow's Son, and the Woman Who Loved Much

points: John came neither eating bread nor drinking wine, and they said he hath a devil; the Son of man came eating and drinking, and they called him a gluttonous man. But wisdom is justified of all her children.

note.label: Luke 7: Great Faith, the Widow's Son, and the Woman Who Loved Much

points: Herod is perplexed, hearing that John was risen from the dead, or that Elias had appeared, and says, John have I beheaded: but who is this?

note.label: Luke 9: The Twelve Sent, the Confession, and the Cost of Following

points: Lord, teach us to pray, as John also taught his disciples. He gives them the words: Our Father which art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name.

note.label: Luke 11: How to Pray, the Strong Man, and the Woes

points: People like to say that John the Baptist was evil, started his own camp, and went against Christ, which is complete nonsense. Let's see what the Bible says. This is the righteous response when you understand that God is using someone or something greater for the same goal: raising up the elect of God so we can inherit the kingdom.

They came unto John and said, Rabbi, he that was with thee beyond Jordan, behold, the same baptizeth, and all men come to him. John answered, A man can receive nothing, except it be given him from heaven. Why is it hard for these other camps to accept that the great work that started from a mustard seed out of a man's living room in 2003 has grown to be this great tree with many branches, and it ain't done yet? Because of envy and hatred. But John the Baptist, the same man you said was not in the truth, accepted it.

note.label: The Inevitability of Obsolescence & Agony of Defeat

points: John's disciples notice that all men are coming to Jesus, and John answers, A man can receive nothing, except it be given him from heaven.

note.label: John 3: Nicodemus, the Serpent Lifted Up, and Who the World Is

points: Jesus himself baptized not, but his disciples, many of whom had begun with John.

note.label: John 4: The Woman at the Well and the Nobleman's Son

points: But I have greater witness than that of John: the works which the Father hath given me to finish bear witness of me.

note.label: John 5: The Pool of Bethesda and the Witness to the Son

points: John truly baptized with water, but they would be baptized with the Holy Ghost not many days hence. There is a distinction between what John taught and what Christ brought.

Baptism comes from the word baptizo, out of the purification laws. John was of the tribe of Levi, his father Zacharias a priest and his mother Elizabeth of the daughters of Aaron, so his water baptism was always symbolic, a preparation leading up to Christ.

John said he must decrease and Christ must increase, and that happens in increments. Two of John's own disciples heard Christ and followed him, which is why in Acts the disciples were still baptizing with water even though Christ himself baptized not with water but with the Holy Ghost. When you believe on Christ as the scripture says, rivers of living water flow out of your belly, meaning wisdom and understanding flow out of the mind that consumes and filters information; but that Holy Ghost was not yet given because Jesus was not yet glorified.

note.label: Acts 1: The Promise of the Father and the Kingdom Restored to Israel

points: When John had first preached before his coming the baptism of repentance to all the people of Israel. All the people of Israel.

note.label: Give Diligence
